headline: High: ComfyUI can expose local model/workflow files to a prompt-leakage target, while both agents lack documented isolation or verification controls.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI can ingest workflow/files and has an asynchronous queue system, so attacker-controlled content could be embedded in inputs. system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage, making it a plausible sink if it consumes ComfyUI outputs. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly evidenced.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into system_prompts_leaks prompts or files
IF a shared workspace or manual copy-paste bridge is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable any automatic import of ComfyUI workflow files into the other agent
Use a manual review step before passing outputs across agents
Label all cross-agent content as untrusted
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI is documented as fully offline except vendor-only egress, and system_prompts_leaks has network egress none. With no shared filesystem or authenticated workspace documented, direct leakage is not established. The main risk is operator-mediated transfer of images, workflows, or model artifacts between the two.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive images or workflows into both agents' reachable files
IF a shared OS workspace is created outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Keep separate directories for each agent
Do not copy sensitive media into shared folders
Review file-sharing permissions before launch
Use local-only storage for any transferred artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI cannot write the filesystem, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses, and system_prompts_leaks has no documented write or mutable-resource capabilities. With no overlapping write surface or shared mutable resource, a capability conflict pathway is not plausible from the profiles.
conditions: IF either profile is updated to add write access to the same directory
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the documented capabilities
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible
Avoid mounting the same writable directory
Do not grant shared OAuth or git credentials
Document any future write scopes before pairing
requires-engineering: add lock-based coordination if writes are later enabled

D_cascading_error.rationale: ComfyUI can produce workflows, images, and model artifacts that another agent may treat as authoritative inputs. system_prompts_leaks is thematically about prompt leakage, so if it consumes ComfyUI output without verification, errors can cascade into misleading downstream content. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF system_prompts_leaks uses ComfyUI-generated artifacts as trusted input
IF no human verification step exists between generation and downstream use
mitigations: Add a verification step before reuse of ComfyUI outputs
Require source labels on all transferred artifacts
Reject outputs that lack provenance metadata
Limit downstream actions to read-only review
requires-engineering: implement structured validation of cross-agent inputs

E_compliance.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, audio, and model artifacts, which can include regulated content, while system_prompts_leaks has no documented residency or retention controls. No direct compliance mismatch is evidenced, but the pair could create policy gaps if sensitive media or prompts are moved between them. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise handling, not a single-agent residency issue.
conditions: IF regulated media or prompts are transferred between the agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ in the deployment environment
mitigations: Classify transferred media before use
Avoid moving regulated content across the pair
Set a short retention window for shared artifacts
Review logging settings for both agents
requires-engineering: align retention and deletion policies
